name: Contact centre agent, seasonal/term (Canada Revenue Agency)
summary: The CRA hires temporary call-centre agents each year to answer taxpayers' phone questions, ramping up before tax season.
whatYouDo: You answer calls from individuals and businesses about taxes and benefits, look up accounts and explain CRA rules, following strict privacy and security procedures. Terms are often seasonal (around January to spring) and may be renewed.
appeal: Federal government employer; large seasonal hiring (aimed for ~1,700 hires for the 2026 season)
2022 remote call-centre roles paid $53,000–$58,000/yr starting, with equipment and training provided
Entry route into the public service; high school diploma level in past postings
Roles exist in English, French and bilingual
watchOuts: Temporary by design; union says ~3,300 call-centre jobs were lost since May 2024 (CRA disputes part of that)
Whether current postings allow telework is not confirmed; remote evidence is from 2022
Phone-heavy work with frustrated callers during peak season

credentials: secondary school diploma or CRA-approved alternative (2022 posting)

training.notes: 2022 releases: training and equipment provided by the CRA.

compensation.notes: Starting salaries in a 2022 CRA news release for remote call-centre roles; stale, check current poster.

reliability.notes: Seasonal terms; CRA rehires for peak season (Dec 2025 coverage) but cut many call-centre staff 2024–2025.

applicationSteps: Create a candidate profile on the CRA careers site
Search CRA postings for contact-centre / client-service roles, especially in the fall before tax season
Check each poster for location, telework, language and term length
Questions: CRA Job Opportunities Helpdesk 1-800-571-7150 (weekdays 8am–8pm ET)
fitsIf: You want a government-employer phone job with decent pay and can handle seasonal terms and busy call queues.
notFitIf: You need guaranteed year-round or fully remote work, or dislike phone work.
